title: Choose exact words for a uniform-exchange composition
instructions: Composition practice. The prompt: ‘Write about a time you helped to improve something in your school or neighbourhood.’ You are writing about your class's used-uniform exchange. Your notes: parents donated 140 used uniform items; volunteers sorted the items by size and pinned a size card to each rack; on the first morning, families waited in one long queue at a single table; on the second morning, a second table opened; over the two mornings, 52 families took at least one item; some sizes for older students ran out by noon on the second morning. Choose the words and sentences you would write, using only what your notes show. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which THREE phrases are exact enough to use and match your notes?

options.text: sorted the items by size
did some stuff with the clothes
52 families took at least one item
the whole town loved it
pinned a size card to each rack

choice_rationales.A: It names the action and how it was done, and the notes record it.
choice_rationales.B: ‘Did some stuff’ hides the action, so the reader cannot picture it.
choice_rationales.C: It gives the recorded number and the exact result.
choice_rationales.D: The notes record 52 families, not the opinion of a whole town.
choice_rationales.E: It names a specific, recorded action that a reader can picture.

parts.hint: Choose phrases that let a reader picture the action and that the notes can support.
parts.correct_explanation: Exact phrases name the real action or result and stay within what the notes show.

parts.prompt: Which word best completes your sentence? ‘Parents ______ 140 used uniform items.’

options.text: made
donated
bestowed
threw in

choice_rationales.A: Parents did not make the items, so the meaning is wrong.
choice_rationales.B: It means gave freely for a good cause, which is exactly what happened, and it suits a school composition.
choice_rationales.C: It is too formal and ceremonial for giving used uniforms.
choice_rationales.D: It is too casual and suggests the items were given carelessly.

parts.hint: Check the meaning first, then check that the word suits a clear school composition.
parts.correct_explanation: ‘Donated’ gives the exact meaning in a natural, plain register.

parts.prompt: Which phrase best completes your sentence? ‘On the first morning, there was ______ at the only table.’

options.text: a big crowd of chaos
a massive jam of humans
a long queue
a lengthy line-up of persons

choice_rationales.A: ‘Crowd of chaos’ is not a natural word partnership, and the notes do not mention chaos.
choice_rationales.B: The words are casual and do not usually go together.
choice_rationales.C: ‘Long queue’ is a natural partnership and matches the notes.
choice_rationales.D: The words are stiff and unnatural; ‘persons’ sounds like an official notice.

parts.hint: Say each option inside the sentence. Which words naturally go together?
parts.correct_explanation: ‘A long queue’ is the natural phrase, and it says exactly what the notes record.

parts.prompt: Which pair of sentences keeps the reader clear about what you are describing?

options.text: Volunteers sorted the uniforms by size. Families then chose uniforms from the racks.
Volunteers sorted the uniforms by size. Families then chose textile goods from the racks.
Volunteers sorted the uniforms by size. Families then chose things from the racks.
Volunteers sorted the uniforms by size. Families then chose fine garments from the racks.

choice_rationales.A: Repeating ‘uniforms’ keeps the reader sure that the same items are meant.
choice_rationales.B: ‘Textile goods’ changes the register and makes the reader wonder if new items are meant.
choice_rationales.C: ‘Things’ is vague and loses the link to the uniforms.
choice_rationales.D: ‘Fine garments’ adds praise the notes do not support and sounds unnatural.

parts.hint: Repeating a key word can be clearer than swapping it for a different word.
parts.correct_explanation: Keeping the key word ‘uniforms’ holds the meaning steady; a forced synonym can blur it.

parts.prompt: Which result sentence stays within your notes?

options.text: The exchange changed the life of every family in the neighbourhood and solved the uniform problem for good.
Over the two mornings, 52 families took at least one item, although some sizes for older students ran out.
Every family that came found exactly the uniform it wanted in the right size on the very first morning.
The exchange was really great and super successful, and everybody who came along was extremely happy with it.

choice_rationales.A: The notes do not show every family's life changing or the problem ending for good.
choice_rationales.B: It gives the recorded number and time, and it admits the shortage.
choice_rationales.C: The notes say some sizes ran out, so this is not true.
choice_rationales.D: The words are vague and too strong, and no one recorded how happy people were.

parts.hint: Prefer the recorded numbers and limits to broad claims about success.
parts.correct_explanation: Numbers, times and limits are exact only when they come from the notes.

parts.prompt: Which paragraph would be the best one to write, with exact words all the way through?

options.text: Parents gave loads of stuff, and we did some things with it so it looked nice. The first morning was a bit of a mess with all the people, so we got another table going. Lots of families came and got stuff. Some sizes ran out, but it was still really good.
Benevolent guardians bestowed copious garments, whereupon our team executed a comprehensive optimisation of apparel logistics and achieved a magnificent outcome for the community.

Parents donated 140 used uniform items. We sorted them by size and pinned a size card to each rack. On the first morning there was a long queue at the only table, so we opened a second table the next day. Over the two mornings, 52 families took at least one item, although some sizes for older students ran out.

Parents donated 300 used uniform items. We sorted them by size and pinned a size card to each rack. The second table removed every queue, every family found the right size, and the exchange solved the uniform problem in our neighbourhood for good. Over the two mornings, every family in the neighbourhood took at least one item.

choice_rationales.A: The paragraph uses vague words such as ‘stuff’, ‘things’ and ‘nice’ in place of the recorded actions and results.
choice_rationales.B: Inflated words hide the simple actions and include unnatural word partnerships.
choice_rationales.C: The words are specific and natural, and every claim stays within the notes.
choice_rationales.D: It invents a number and makes claims about every family and a permanent result that the notes do not support.

parts.hint: Choose the paragraph that makes the facts clear without vague words, showy words or exaggeration.
parts.correct_explanation: Exact vocabulary matches the meaning, uses natural word partnerships, suits a school composition and stays within the evidence.
